note: Literature on GTF3C3-related neurodevelopmental disorder indicates simplified gyral pattern is reported in only a subset/single patient (e.g., 1 of 4 patients in Abdel-Hamid 2025), supporting that it occurs in <30% of cases and is an infrequent, severe-spectrum feature rather than a core hallmark.

evidence.text: In a cohort of four patients from three unrelated families with biallelic GTF3C3 variants, brain imaging demonstrated brain atrophy with predominant cerebellar involvement and hypoplasia of frontal lobes, but only one patient presented with moderate to severe simplified gyral pattern.

source.title: Biallelic variants in GTF3C3 encoding a subunit of the TFIIIC2 complex are associated with neurodevelopmental phenotypes in humans and zebrafish
source.quote: Their brain imaging showed brain atrophy with predominant cerebellar involvement, as well as hypoplasia of the frontal lobes and one patient had moderate to severe simplified gyral pattern.

evidence.text: A review of white matter and neurodevelopmental disorders caused by TFIIIC subunits notes cerebellar hypoplasia and a simplified gyral pattern reported in only one patient with GTF3C3 mutations.
